header.running_head: The Enthusiasm of the Sahabah (RA) to Die and Give their Lives in the path of Allaah

blocks.text: (RA), who was the maternal grandfather of Hadhrat Aasim bin Umar bin Khattaab (RA). The expedition proceeded and was at a place between Usfaan and Makkah when their presence was reported to a clan from the Hudhayl tribe known as the Banu Lihyaan. With close to a hundred archers, the people of this tribe set out after the Sahabah (RA) and traced their tracks until they arrived at a place where the Sahabah (RA) had set up camp earlier. There they found some date stones from the provisions that the Sahabah (RA) had brought from Madinah. Seeing this, they said, "These are dates from Yathrib." They then continued tracing the tracks until they eventually caught up with the Sahabah (RA).

Hadhrat Aasim (RA) and his companions took shelter on a hillock as the Banu Lihyaan surrounded them. The Banu Lihyaan called out, "We make a promise that we shall not kill any of you if you surrender to us." Hadhrat Aasim (RA) said, "As for myself, I shall never surrender into the custody of a Kaafir." He then prayed, "O Allaah! Inform Your Nabi ﷺ about us." The Sahabah (RA) then fought the Banu Lihyaan, who martyred Hadhrat Aasim (RA) and another seven Sahabah (RA) with arrows. The only ones who survived were Hadhrat Khubayb, Hadhrat Zaid and another Sahabi (RA).

When the Banu Lihyaan again offered their promise, these Sahabah (RA) agreed to it and came down from the hillock. However, no sooner did the Banu Lihyaan have control over them then they removed the strings from their bows and used it to tie the Sahabah (RA) up. To this, the third Sahabi (RA) said, "This is the first breach of your promise." He then refused to accompany them. Despite their efforts to pull and drag him, he would not budge. They eventually killed him.

They then took Hadhrat Khubayb (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid (RA) away and sold them in Makkah. The sons of Haarith bin Aamir bin Naufal bought Hadhrat Khubayb (RA) because he had killed (their father) Haarith bin Aamir in the Battle of Badr. He lived as a prisoner with them until they eventually decided to kill him. Hadhrat Khubayb (RA) asked one of the ladies of the household for a razor to shave with and she lent it to him. (Narrating the incident later) She says, "I was unmindful of one of my little children who went towards him. When the child came to him, he put the child on his lap. When I saw this, I became terribly alarmed for he was holding the razor in his hand (I thought that he would use the razor to kill the child). Sensing fear, he said, "Are you afraid that I will kill this child? By the will of Allaah, I shall never do such a thing."

The lady narrates further, "I have never seen a prisoner better than Hadhrat Khubayb (RA). I saw him eating a bunch of grapes at a time when there was no fruit in Makkah and he was bound in chains. It was nothing short of (unseen) sustenance that Allaah had provided for him."

When Hadhrat Khubayb (RA) was led outside the area of the Haram to be executed, he requested to be left to perform two Rakaahs of salaah. After performing the salaah, he turned to the people and said, "I would have lengthened the salaah if it were not for you thinking that (I am doing so because)
